purpose: Held-out test evaluation of the GC10-DET checkpoint (Gap 8: roll-mark and edge-defect coverage). Training only; this report does not train anything.

training_curve.note: best.pt is the epoch-53 checkpoint (ultralytics saves best-by-val-mAP50), not the epoch-70 checkpoint. Both are close (0.5506 vs 0.5494), so there is no real overfitting signal in the last 17 epochs.

dataset_verification.method: Independent recount from data/gc10-det/{split}/labels/*.txt, plus SHA-256 content hashing and filename-derived line-scan sequence IDs on data/gc10-det/{split}/images/*, run fresh (not read from manifest.json).

disjointness_check.method: SHA-256 content hash of every image file, plus a line-scan sequence id parsed from the filename (img_<camera>_<sequence>_<frame>), computed independently of manifest.json

dataset_verification.verdict: All counts, class mapping, and split disjointness claims in reports/gc10_dataset.md are confirmed by independent recount and rehashing. No discrepancy found.

test_evaluation.command: yolo detect val model=models/yolov8n_gc10_640/weights/best.pt data=data/gc10-det/data.yaml split=test imgsz=640 batch=16 device=mps conf=0.001 iou=0.7
test_evaluation.reproducibility_note: Identical numbers obtained across the ultralytics Python API (model.val(...)), the yolo CLI, and a fresh re-run in a separate verification pass. iou=0.7 is the 'ultralytics validator defaults' value used by every other val run in this project (reports/evaluation.json's own protocol field names it explicitly); an earlier draft of this report used iou=0.6 without documenting why, which moved overall mAP50 from 0.582 to 0.592. Corrected here to iou=0.7 for consistency with the rest of the project. Both runs are reproducible from reports/gc10_coverage.md's 'Reproducing this report' section.

roll_marks.confidence_statement: Both classes are thin enough that a single flipped box changes the headline number by more than a rounding error: rolled_pit has 13 test instances, so one instance moving from miss to hit changes recall by 1/13 = 7.7 points; crease has 11, so one flip changes recall by 1/11 = 9.1 points. AP50 on 11-13 instances does not support a claim tighter than 'roughly a fifth to a third, weak, and the number itself is unstable.' The project's earlier bootstrap on NEU-DET (446 test boxes) reported a +/-0.025 half-width; nothing this small can be narrower than the effect it claims.

edge_defects_proxy.confidence_statement: 40 and 21 test instances respectively are enough to trust the direction of these numbers (strong), though still thinner than the shipped model's 446-box NEU-DET test set. These are NOT edge cracks: crescent_gap is a scalloped bite out of the strip edge and waist_fold is a folded-over edge, both edge-region geometry defects. waist_fold's median box covers 33.8% of the frame (per reports/gc10_dataset.md section 6), so its high AP50 partly reflects that a large box is easy to overlap at IoU 0.5; crescent_gap (5.3% median area) is the more meaningful of the two localisation-wise.

sanity_check_predictions.command: model.predict(source=<image>, imgsz=640, conf=0.15, device=mps) via ultralytics.YOLO, weights=models/yolov8n_gc10_640/weights/best.pt

images.assessment: crescent_gap box overlaps the ground-truth box (gt approx [474,218,782,821]) closely and at a strong confidence. weld_line is an unlabelled second detection on this frame -- plausibly a real weld seam GC10 did not annotate here, not checked against ground truth.

Right region and right class, but three overlapping boxes at low, closely-spaced confidence (0.18-0.32) where one clean box is warranted -- exactly the low-confidence, imprecise-localisation behaviour the 0.30 AP50 predicts, not a clean detection.

weld_line box matches its ground truth closely. The rolled_pit box in this same image (small, top-right corner) was MISSED ENTIRELY at conf 0.15 -- no detection of any class in that region. This is a real, representative failure, not a cherry-picked one: see the 11-image rolled_pit sweep below.

Correct class, single clean box, substantial overlap with ground truth (gt approx [294,128,1609,951]) though smaller than the full labelled region -- consistent with waist_fold's known 'large-region label' character.

rolled_pit_broad_sweep.note: All 11 GC10 test images containing a rolled_pit ground-truth box, at conf=0.15, to check whether the single miss above was representative or a one-off.
rolled_pit_broad_sweep.command: model.predict(source=<image>, imgsz=640, conf=0.15, device=mps) for each of the 11 rolled_pit test images
rolled_pit_broad_sweep.summary: 4 of 11 images produce zero rolled_pit detections at conf 0.15 (image-level miss). The remaining 7 produce at least one, but confidences cluster low (0.16-0.71, median approx 0.34) and box counts do not always match instance counts (e.g. 2 predicted vs 1 gt, or 3 vs 2). This is a genuinely weak, low-confidence class in practice, matching the AP50 0.1126 / recall 0.2308 measured on the full test split -- not an artefact of the metric.

honesty_notes: No edge-crack class exists in GC10-DET or in this checkpoint. crescent_gap and waist_fold are edge-region geometry proxies, not cracks. This checkpoint has never seen a labelled crack of any kind.

rolled_pit and crease are trained and measured, but on 13 and 11 test instances respectively. The AP50 numbers (0.11, 0.29) are real, reproducible, and weak -- this is not a measurement problem, the broad sweep above shows the model genuinely misses or under-confidently detects these on individual images.

waist_fold's strong AP50 (0.84) is partly inflated by box size: its median ground-truth box covers a third of the frame, which is easy to overlap at IoU 0.5. crescent_gap's 0.92 is the more meaningful of the two edge-family numbers.

This checkpoint is NOT merged with the shipped model or the joint model. It stands alone, at models/yolov8n_gc10_640/weights/best.pt, evaluated only against GC10's own held-out test split. resolve_weights() is untouched; nothing about deployment changes as a result of this report.
